  • Answer
  • As the dataset size increases, the number of comparisons required by linear search and
  • binary search changes differently. As the dataset size increases, the number of comparisons
  • required by linear search and binary search changes differently.
  • • Linear Search
  • o Checks each element one by one until the target is found.
  • o As the dataset grows, the number of comparisons increases linearly
  • (proportional to n).
  • o Worst-case time complexity: O(n).
  • • Binary Search
  • o Works only on a sorted dataset.
  • o Divides the search space into two halves after each comparison.
  • o As the dataset grows, the number of comparisons increases very slowly
  • (logarithmically).
  • o Worst-case time complexity: O(log₂ n).
  • For small datasets, both methods may perform similarly. However, as the dataset becomes
  • larger, binary search requires far fewer comparisons than linear search, making it much
  • more efficient for searching in sorted data.

  • Answer
  • As the dataset size increases, the number of comparisons required by linear search and
  • binary search changes differently. As the dataset size increases, the number of comparisons
  • required by linear search and binary search changes differently.
  • • Linear Search
  • o Checks each element one by one until the target is found.
  • o As the dataset grows, the number of comparisons increases linearly
  • (proportional to n).
  • o Worst-case time complexity: O(n).
  • • Binary Search
  • o Works only on a sorted dataset.
  • o Divides the search space into two halves after each comparison.
  • o As the dataset grows, the number of comparisons increases very slowly
  • (logarithmically).
  • o Worst-case time complexity: O(log₂ n).
  • For small datasets, both methods may perform similarly. However, as the dataset becomes
  • larger, binary search requires far fewer comparisons than linear search, making it much
  • more efficient for searching in sorted data.

questions.question: Define circular queue and list its basic operations.
questions.solution_html:
• Answer
  • A Circular Queue is a queue in which the last position is connected back to the first position
  • forming a circle. It follows the FIFO (First In First Out) principle and efficiently utilizes
  • memory by reusing empty spaces created after deletions.
  • Need for Circular Queue (2 Marks)
  • In a linear queue, after several dequeue operations, empty spaces at the beginning cannot be
  • reused.
  • A circular queue overcomes this problem by allowing the rear pointer to wrap around to the
  • beginning of the array.
  • Array Representation (2 Marks)
  • • Queue is stored in an array.
  • • Two pointers are maintained
  • o Front → points to the first element.
  • o Rear → points to the last element.
  • Initially
  • Front = Rear = -1
  • Basic Operations (6 Marks)
